correctness.rationale: The bitangency criterion is an iff: a binary quartic on a rational line has all even geometric zero multiplicities iff it is a nonzero F_7 scalar times a quadratic square. Exactly 57 rational lines and 32 published model equations define a finite exhaustive census. Inspected both source implementations: five-value degree-four interpolation/square signatures and independent polynomial factor exponent plus infinity parity with Gröbner smoothness on all affine charts. Independently evaluated both D4 witness curves: b(C4)=4 and b(C8)=8 with precisely the asserted normalized line normals and no F_7 points. Full 32-vector histogram matches stored dual-code outputs, but was not independently executed in this run; source algebra and finite exhaustive algorithm support the complete claim, conditional on Faber–Grantham–Howe input classification. The shared Weil comparison uses F7, F49, F343 point counts/Newton identities; numerical Weil pair was not recomputed independently here.
